utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. Today is Thursday, 10th of September, 2009. I would like to greet Mr. Seselj. I would like to greet our colleagues from the Prosecution, Mr. Marcussen and Ms. Biersay, and I would like to greet their associates. And I would also like to greet all the staff helping us in this courtroom. Mr. Seselj, we are holding this hearing today despite the fact that last time I had said to you that we would meet again in October, given that there were not many courtrooms available since several trials are being held at the same time. In the meantime, on the 27th of August, 2009, the Prosecutor issued a public request with confidential annexes regarding the issue of your representation. The Prosecutor wanted the Chamber to impose a counsel on you. We have looked into this motion and I hope that it was translated into your language, and the Chamber felt that we had to see you very quickly in order to see whether you are planning to answer to this motion either by written submissions or by having an oral submission. But from a personal point of view, I have to say that given the importance of this motion, I do believe that it will be highly advisable for you to make written submissions. Why? Well, because it could be possible for the Chamber of Appeals that -- for the Chamber of Appeals to be either seized by the Prosecutor or by yourself. So we are holding this hearing to see what is your intention as regards this motion and, of course, to give you the floor if you have other issues to touch upon. So, Mr. Seselj, I give you the floor regarding this motion to impose a counsel on you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How can I respond to that request since I did not receive it, Your Honour? I was never issued with that request. I heard that in the press there were articles dealing with the matter and with the request that was resubmitted by the Prosecution; however, I have not received that request. In principle, I think that such a request on the part of the OTP is nothing less than abuse of the proceedings. The OTP is asking for the impossible. They are asking for my right to defence be taken away from me. This is not possible in a civilised world. I can be the worst of criminals, it is already assumed that I am criminal, and that's why I'm on trial. I could have even breached procedural rules; however, for as long as I behave in an articulate and normal manner in the courtroom, you cannot deprive me of my right to defence. In other words, my behaviour in the courtroom should be non-articulated, immoral, in other words, such as to prevent a normal proceedings. In this courtroom, you have not encountered such behaviour. You may have been cross with me when I told you something that you didn't want to hear, that was unpleasant for your ears, you could have felt hurt; however, you cannot deny that everything that was said was part of a very civilised communication process. I have never prevented normal procedure, and since I have never done that you cannot deprive me of my right to defence. The press says that one of the arguments on the side of the Prosecution is the fact that I have been convicted of contempt of court. Can you see how unprofessional the OTP are? They don't have any clue about the law. That conviction is still not valid. I have announced that I will appeal and my appeal is pending. I'm going to file my appeal within the stipulated dead-line. The OTP cannot invoke that conviction until it becomes valid. And even if it was valid, this is not a valid argument for them to deprive me of my right to defence, because the book that I was convicted for was published before the start of this trial, and if this book jeopardises this trial, then you have to annul the entire course of the trial so far. Let's put this aside. The fact that that conviction is against the law that in no serious court of law it could be upheld. I have been convicted for its contents, and its contents consist of a number of documents, none of the documents that I myself authored. First of all, you -- there are my submission to the Trial Chamber which are public. My objections to the indictment which are public. The paper -- you don't have the patience to listen to me? Well, very well, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not want to interrupt you. First of all, you are telling us that you haven't received or read this motion. We are on the 10th of September. The submissions were made on the 27th of August, so it's almost two weeks ago, so I don't understand why this has not been translated and brought to your attention. So it goes without saying that it will be upon the date of receipt of this motion that you will be in a position to send your submissions or to let us know that you have the intention to answer. That is for one. Secondly, we are not here to talk again about the trial of the Trial Chamber II. The Appeals Chamber is looking into your appeal and no sentence or no decision has been made. This is clear for everyone. Just to clarify this, and you have touched upon the issue based on press articles, and for once they were well informed. The main basis for this motion is that you were sentenced of contempt of court, and as far as the Prosecution is concerned, it bears some consequences; namely, that you should not be able to carry on defending yourself. And, therefore, we should impose a counsel on you. This is the point of view of the Prosecution which is developed in their written submissions. And this is on this that I would like or that the Chamber would like for you to answer either by written submissions or by an oral position. And my colleague is going to add some points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I wanted to have some point of clarification. I would like to point out that this is not a motion from August. It's an additional document from a motion. Unfortunately, I do not remember the date of this other motion. Have you not received the first motion? Or are you saying that you have not received the additional documents to this motion?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have not received the motion and I've not even been aware of the existence of any additional documents. Judging by the press, that was towards the end of August. That's when that motion was made public on the internet, but not in its entirety. As far as I've been informed, some of the parts of that motion have not even been made available to the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask a couple of questions to the Prosecution. So I would like Mr. Marcussen to clarify some points. I would like to know whether the motion of the 27th of August, 2009, is a real motion which would come as an addition to previous motions on which the Chamber had decided to postpone their decision, or as my colleague was saying, was there a motion prior to the 27th of August? So Ms. Biersay or Mr. Marcussen, could you answer that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Yes, what we filed in August was a supplement to the Prosecution's motion dated the 28th of July, 2008. Now, I'm having this verified, but from memory, there are three versions of that motion filed, and ex parte confidential version; a confidential version, which the accused should have received; and a public version. Now I think it might simply be due to the fact that quite a long time has past and maybe the accused has forgotten that motion was filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Seselj, given that I know the procedure very well, I have no right to make any mistake. When I talked about the motion of the 27th of August, I thought that it was a new motion which was in addition to prior motions, but there wasn't a motion that would have been issued before July or before June, so I was referring to all prior motions. But as far as I'm concerned, it's very clear now, and I would like to thank the Prosecution for having clarified that, as far as they are concerned, and I agree with them, the main motion was dated 28th of July, 2008, and the -- this motion is an additional motion compared to the main motion. So this is why I'm asking you, given that you were aware of the previous motions, if you -- I'm asking you whether you are planning to answer to the motion of the 27th of August, but given you've just told us that you have not received it, it is becoming difficult because I cannot really go any further. First of all, you have to peruse all the paragraphs of this motion, and then you can voice your point of view, given that this motion is a 2.545 words and has 34 paragraphs, it will take awhile. 2.545 words.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I be permitted to say something else? First of all, I've not forgotten anything. If anybody forgets something in this courtroom, it's the OTP, not me. I remember very well the request that was filed on the 28th of July last year and I responded orally to that request. And that request also had a lot of ex parte parts. It seems that this annex or addition of which I hear the first time, I hear for the first time that the new motion is in the form of an addition to the request that was filed a year ago. And that new motion also has ex parte parts. Here we are not talking about whether I'm going to respond or not. The question that is raised here is whether you, as Judges, will permit yourself to look at a motion with a lot of ex parte details and decide on my essential procedural right. You have a motion filed by the OTP to which I cannot respond because I'm not aware of all of its parts, because they are all ex parte. They are eternally secret and confidential for me, and you have to make a decision. This is a Kafka-like process. If you agree to decide on that motion with its ex parte parts, then you have accepted to be in charge of a Kafkian process. I don't know what to respond to and I will not respond to the OTP motions that have ex parte parts or ex parte additions. I will never, ever again do that. I'm not interested in such motions and request. They are not existent for me. And as for you, you do whatever; it's up to you. You know that I have not expected anything good from you in principle and that hasn't changed. You do whatever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I cannot let you say -- well, you know, you have a great deal of freedom of speech and I will never argue against that, but when you say, I do not expect anything good from you, I'm actually flabbergasted as to what I hear from you. I have to say, I'm astonished. You expected from Judges to issue informed decisions and if you don't agree, you can make appeal. By saying this, you actually suspect that we are partial against you, and I cannot let this happen and I cannot let this be said. Please wait and see. There is a motion that has been filed by the Prosecutor, for what its worth. You will say what you have to say and the Chamber will hand down a decision, and you will wait and you will see what happens. If the decision is not in your agreement, then you can make appeal. If you are happy with the decision, then you say nothing. So before you decide on our behaviour preemptively, wait and see. We cannot really go any further on this issue since you have not been made aware of the motion, and I invite the translation services to be quick.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I? Mr. President, a majority of the members of this Trial Chamber have already made a decision on staying these proceedings and their decision also has a lot of ex parte parts, so I've never learned of all the arguments that were used in making the decision on putting this trial on hold for a number of months. How can I appeal against somebody if I'm not aware of what it is that I have to appeal against? I value all that, but I'm looking at you as a Trial Chamber as a whole and I'm looking at you as a materialised Hague Tribunal here in this courtroom. For me you are The Hague Tribunal. It is you that I meet as The Hague Tribunal and you know only too well what I think about The Hague Tribunal. I've never hidden that. And this is the integral part of the strategy of my Defence. On every occasion that I have, I emphasise what I think about The Hague Tribunal. So I don't see that there's any reason for anybody to be surprised. If you again reach a decision based on the request that contains ex parte parts and ex parte additions, and then if your decision also contains new ex parte parts, what are we talking about? You can find this only in Kafka. I've not encountered that in any law book. I have only found this in Franz Kafka's novel. I have not encountered that anywhere else. You are making a decision on the request of the -- of which I'm not aware. It is impossible anywhere else. Not in Italy, not in Denmark, not in France. In the proceedings against me, there shouldn't be a single secret. The Rules of Procedure and Evidence enable temporary confidentiality when it comes to the protection of the witnesses, but at the end of the day, I have to be disclosed all that. How can there be secrets for me in the proceedings that are conducted against me? It's impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, thanks for your viewpoints. You know very well, being a lawyer, that ex parte submissions in criminal proceedings is not uncommon. It exists in Danish law, in French law, in Italian law, and even in your own system. So that should not come as a surprise to you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me, the interpretation is missing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There may be ex parte motions, but they concern some urgent measures that have to be taken. And it's impossible to conduct a trial with ex parte portions thereof. That's impossible. So if a party files a motion ex parte asking you to do something to prevent some negative effects or to prevent something that might cause irreparable damage, and it demands an urgent response on your part, that's okay. And usually they are filed in the pre-trial stage. Once the trial begins, please explain to me in Danish criminal law what can be done ex parte, and in such a way that defence is never made aware of the contents. Here we are talking about my fundamental right. I either am entitled to defend myself or not. The fact that you are constantly being pushed and pressurised to assign counsel to me, well, it's been calculated in order to strip me of my right to defend myself because nobody, no Defence counsel that you could assign to me would not be able to defend me properly. You would assign to me a spy from the OTP who would do everything they could to argue in favour of the Prosecution and to conduct this trial as has been planned, and there's no other way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, let me speak for my own part, and I do not know the position of my fellow Judges, but I have been quite impressed by the way in which you have been able to defend yourself, and as of this moment, no decision has been made to impose counsel on you. The Prosecution has filed a submission to have such counsel imposed because of the fact that you have been convicted of contempt, and the meeting today was called because the Chamber wanted to hear your position on that issue. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Seselj, do you want to conclude on this topic? I fully share what Judge Harhoff has just said. He has told you exactly what is the situation at this stage. Until now, the Chamber has not imposed a counsel on you, as you are aware. Secondly, the Prosecutor has filed a motion on the 27th of August. We are waiting for your position on this motion, and the Chamber will hands down a decision. So you cannot pre-empt our decision in one way or another.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not intend, Mr. President, to pre-empt your decision. As regards the assignment of Defence counsel to me, you do know what my general view is, what my position is, and you know what I am prepared to do to defend my right to defend myself, to safe-guard it. If you deliver to me a Prosecution motion or an addendum to a motion with ex parte parts, let me tell you in advance, I do not have any intention to responds to that. I'm not interested in any OTP motions with ex parte parts. For as long as I'm not able to read the entirety of the motion, that motion is non-existent. I will sign -- I will confirm the receipt of the motion in Serbian but I will not respond to it, so you can rule right away. Why should you wait for me respond if I tell you in advance that I will not respond to any motions that contain ex parte parts? There's no reason for you to wait. You can rule immediately. You can rule today, in fact. I have told you what the repercussions will be of a decision which might possibly, let me stress possibly might, strip me of my right to defend myself and I have let you know what it is. I hope that you are aware of it, and I hope that as professional Judges, as professional -- as law professionals who are well regarded in your countries, that you are aware that there is no foundation whatsoever, no reason whatsoever for you to strip me of my right to defend myself, and that nobody who would appear here in this courtroom to figure as my Defence counsel could not do the job. They could not defend me, they would just be a figure head, acting, an actor pretending that they are defending myself. And we have seen such actors play-acting as Defence counsel here in this -- in many courtrooms here, in many trials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, the Registrar's informed me that you will receive translation today of this motion. You have pointed out your position. It's on the transcript. So the Chamber will look into this. You say that if the motion contains ex parte parts, you will not answer this motion. So everything is very clear. This was the main topic that we wanted to handle today with you, and this is why we organised this hearing. So, Mr. Seselj, I would like to know whether there are other topics that you would like to touch upon, bearing in mind that of course we saw each other not so long ago, there are other problems that may have cropped up in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have two things to say to you. First, I have to keep the promise that I gave you, that at every session I will draw your attention to the fact that other fundamental rights that I possess are being violated, primarily the right to be tried expeditiously in a reasonable time, and this has been violated, and I have been here in the Detention Unit for such a long time and also I'm convicted for contempt of court. And I'm discriminated against when you -- in comparison with other people who are on trial here in this manner. Secondly, some ten days ago I filed a request to the Registry, and this regards the next week, Thursday and Friday next week, I asked to be allowed to receive a visit by Zoran Krasic, Slavko Jerkovic, Boris Aleksic, and Marina Raguz as my legal advisors and case managers in the main trial, and Dejan Mirovic as my legal advisor in the contempt of court proceedings. And since a year has passed since the adjournment or, rather, the suspension of two of my legal associates, and prohibiting me from establishing and maintaining proper communications with them, based on a false claim by Tomislav Nikolic that I abused the privileged communication for political ends. Since none of it has been proven, there is not a single shred of evidence that might disqualify either Zoran Krasic or Slavko Jerkovic, I demanded that their status as legal advisors be restored with all the rights that stem from it, and I have yet to receive a response. Secondly, yesterday, the deputy warden of the Detention Unit came and handed me a letter from the Prosecution but took it away afterwards. In this letter the Prosecution demands that I return to them a list of videotapes that they have. It's the 6.600 hours of video recordings that were handed to me, but this was not done in good faith because it was impossible to do so in the conditions that were set up. The Prosecution now tells me that this is a wrong list and I should return it to them so that they can give me the right list. And I have a feeling that the Prosecution now feels bad about giving me the first list because they now informed me that they have some recordings that they don't want me to know about. I haven't yet been able to identify what those tapes are but I have asked my case manager to look into it since the whole list is in Belgrade. And I also told her that she should keep it safe because if the Prosecution asks the pro-Western regime in Belgrade to look for it there, there is no legal foundation for them asking me to return the list to them. If the list was labeled confidential, I will not make it public, but why should I return it to them? Let me remind you that in 2005, at the request of the Prosecution, my cell was raided and documents were seized, documents that the Prosecution itself submitted to me, and they removed some documents that the Prosecution didn't want me to have. And those documents were later on given to the Registry for safekeeping, and I now want to renew my request that those documents be given back to me, the documents that were seized, because I believe those documents to be very important for me case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Seselj. You are touching upon quite a few questions and I'm going to try and list them down so that we don't forget to answer to any of them. This is news to us. You have just told us that you had written to the Registry and you told them that you wanted to meet on Thursday and Friday your legal associates. I would like to know whether the Registry answered or not?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With me, not with them, because the interpretation that I received is that they should meet with them. Not with them, with me. They should meet with me, the Registry has yet to respond to this request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. Very well. So you did not get an answer from the Registry, I understand. It is our opinion -- but let me confer with my fellow Judges and I will tell you immediately what is our position on that meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Seselj, I conferred with me fellow Judges and the Trial Chamber's position is very clear on this. You are absolutely -- you should actually meet your associates. You are perfectly -- you have the right for that. But the Chamber would like to say the following: Concerning Mr. Krasic, the Trial Chamber said that you cannot -- Mr. Krasic concerning Mr. Krasic, the Trial Chamber believes that you cannot tell him any confidential information, but nothing forbids you to meet with him and to inform him on the case. You may talk to him about this trial, of course, but since our decision has been rendered, you cannot communicate to him any confidential information. But there are no -- you don't have that many confidential information anyway, so nothing opposes you. We do not disagree with you meeting with him and the Registry will answer to you on this. And I would like to add that the decision that we had rendered applied also to Mr. Jerkovic. I don't know if on the list that you have given us --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... one word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, there's not a single shred of confidential information that Zoran Krasic has not yet been made aware of, so I would like to somebody to draw my attention to it if there is such piece of information. Even the witness that we heard in closed session in July, Zoran Krasic knows everything about him because documents had been delivered before that. So there is not a single important confidential piece of information that he is not aware of. If the Prosecution now calls a new witness that was not on the initial list requesting full confidentiality, then it would make sense for you to insist that Zoran Krasic should not be made aware of it. But what is the problem now? If you say that Zoran Krasic cannot be told any confidential information, the Registry will use that just as it had the last time, about a year ago, to convene a meeting that is videotaped in a small chamber that looked like a gas chamber after several hours of conversation, because there was not enough air. So what is the point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In any case, the Trial Chamber confirms that you may meet with your associates with the exception of course, of communicating confidential documents, but to my knowledge there were no confidential documents since then. I do not have the entire list, however, but I believe that there weren't any confidential documents. This being said, I am satisfied that the first problem is solved, but of course everything will depend on the answer that the Registry will give you. You know, I'm very -- I believe in transparency. I don't like to hide anything and I was wondering, and I checked the transcript in the Karadzic Pre-Trial Conference, and I checked which were his associates, and while I reread the transcript, I found out that Mr. Karadzic has associates, they are -- they receive a pay and they can come here and the trip is paid. So I think that your associates should get the same rights just like the associates of Mr. Karadzic, with respect to the material question. It is of course very important that everybody gets the same treatment in this Tribunal. But that's of course the Registry's responsibility. Now, about the videos, you told us that the index had been sent to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something in this regard, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you like to react to the index or --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As regards not what you have just said, but actually you raised a new issue that I did not raise at this conference, so I think it would be good for me to follow-up on what you just said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very well, go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Travel expenses for the Defence counsel and members of the Defence team that are allowed to come and visit their client, so far the travel expenses have always been paid by the Registry, and the travel expenses have never been at the expense of the Defence, because the Defence budget, as it is determined and it is for the most part paid by the Registry, did not include -- was not supposed to cover the travel expenses. Those expenses were always supposed to be extra on top of that. And since September last year, when I was visited on one occasion by all of my legal advisors and case managers, and that was that meeting that I was telling you about that was recorded by cameras and in a small airless chamber, that happened only once. After that I was only visited by Mr. Aleksic and Marina Raguz on several occasions and I always had to cover their travel expenses. The Registry refused to cover it. So now I am demanding, since you have now given me an example from Mr. Karadzic's case, from another case before this same Tribunal, that the Trial Chamber should demand from the Registry to cover the travel expenses for my legal advisors and to recompense me for the visits that have not been paid for so far in the past year. I think it would be in line with the practice before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Trial Chamber notes your words and we will give you the adequate answer. Now, with regard to the videos, a couple of months ago you requested to obtain the videos from the Prosecutor. The Prosecutor gathered the videos, you say that you have over 6.000 hours of viewing time. You are surely right. And the Prosecutor sent you also an index. The OTP informed you that there was a mistake and that they will hand you a different or another index, and asked you to return to them the index that you had received so that you may have the exact index and exactly what you had requested. So the situation is as follows: You just informed us that all of this is in Belgrade, therefore, the Prosecutor would like to get all that material so that he can send you a new index. If I understood correctly, and can you please tell me, what is your exact position regarding that problem? You told us already but I would like it to be clear.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether the Prosecution would go and pick up anything anywhere, but I took preemptive measures. If the Prosecution shows up with an armed support by the pro-Western regime in Belgrade, I've taken measures to prevent them from finding it there where I keep the materials that pertain to my trial. But since I am a person -- a good person, I'm always ready for compromise. If they pay back the 250 Euros that the detention administration found and seized from my cell, and I could not find any rule that prohibits explicitly a detainee from having money in their possession, so 250 Euros and also for the 31 sports shirts that were taken away from me, well, you know when it was that I first raised this issue, two and a half years. And if I get the books and the copies of the Velika Serbia journal that were seized by the Detention Unit administration, if I get all that, I will order my legal advisors to bring the whole list here next week and to hand it over to the Prosecution, and I don't need a new one. So you can see that I am a person showing goodwill and very constructive. If I don't get those things that belong to me, the Prosecution will never, ever get the list that they had given me. The list will simply disappear, without a trace. And nobody will be able to determine how it disappeared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, we already knew, of course, but we didn't follow it up. You did tell us a while ago that you had in your possession a certain sum of money, 250 Euros. You say that this sum of money was "seized," I don't really know the exact reason, the exact legal reason for this money being seized. And you've also told us about these jerseys that you had received, somebody had sent them to you and you wanted to distribute them to your fellow detention comrades, and the UNDU did not give you those jerseys. Now, I'm also discovering or I hear you that -- I hear you saying that there are some magazines, Velika Serbia, I don't also know why that was seized and why you were not given these magazines, and so you are telling us that in a spirit of cooperation you are ready to proceed to an exchange. It's the Registry that was in charge of the seizure of this money. I don't know if the rule is against a person having money. Normally in our jurisdictions, the detainee does not have the right to have money on him. He may purchase food but then from an account which is held by the Registry in order to avoid money trafficking within a prison -- within the prison walls. That's of course -- those are the rules. But your request is basically addressed to the Registry. But you know, Mr. Seselj, that the relationship between the Registry and detainee is a relationship that can be -- or you can be -- you can inform the Presiding Judge or the President of the Tribunal if you are not satisfied with the relationship that you would have with the Registry. You may make a written submission and the Registry has the obligation to answer; and if you are not happy with the answer, then you inform the President of the Tribunal. And I would like to remind you that this is a principle that exists, and we also reminded you of this on many occasions. Now, you are making an oral request, in a way. You are asking to get your money back, the magazine, and the jerseys. I can say that this is a motion made to the Registry in a certain way. Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, a few days ago, maybe ten or 15 days ago, I reminded the Registry about the three problems that I've just mentioned, and the Registry replied that that was the discretionary right of the Detention Unit management and that applied to the money, the jerseys, and the books, and Velika Serbia magazine, all of which were seized from me. Why did I present these problems? This is a sign of my goodwill. If the Detention Unit restores my money -- and I never received a general document showing that detainees are not supposed to keep money. It is true that money should be deposited in an account. However, I had a certain sum of money in my cell and the Detention Unit management punished me for that without any disciplinary proceedings. I believe that that was against the law and I insist that these things should be returned to me. I'm talking here about that somebody [as interpreted] that the OTP requests, and it seems that the OTP is very keen on having the file returned to them because they provided something to me within that file, and I don't know what it is, but they obviously know what it is and they don't want me to know what it is. And I'm just asking for three very minor things. 250 Euro, 31 sports jerseys, that will not jeopardise anybody in the detention unit, and a certain number of book that were seized, as well as the copies of the Velika Serbia magazine. Again, these will not jeopardise anybody because all these are public. Those were all published and available to the general public and there was no ban on their distribution. On the one hand, they can do a little thing and return to me what is mine, and they can deal with that problem; and I, on my part, return the file to them. I believe this is fair on my part. If they don't wish to do that, if they want to play tug of war with me, there's no single person in this world who can be more obstinate than me. There's no person in the world more obstinate than me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. All those who have decisionary power will be able to -- a decision of power will be able react to what you said. Now, I don't know if your legal advisors were coming next week if their trip will be paid for. I have no idea. But it looks good so far, and as we said, let's wait for Thursday and Friday and then you will be able to talk to them. They will come and visit you. Now, Mr. Seselj, would you like to raise another issue?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have told you everything that I wanted and had to tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, thank you very much, Mr. Seselj. Mr. Marcussen, I'm very happy to see you again. I know that you are now in charge of the file as regards the OTP, since Mr. Mundis left us. So I would like to give you the floor and you can therefore tell us what are the issues that you would like to raise on behalf of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm at the moment holding the baby, so to speak, but we will see how we will organise this case later on and the Chamber will be informed if needed about the structure of the Prosecution team. As for the issues raised today, I just -- there's one thing I would like to raise, and that's going back to the beginning of what we discussed this day, and that is the issue of the supplement to the Prosecution's motion to terminate the accused's self-representation. I just wanted to update the Trial Chamber on one issue. Of course, as the Chamber has of informed the accused, the basis for the motion or the supplement is that the accused has been convicted for a deliberate breach of protective measures ordered by the Trial Chamber. He has been found guilty and sentenced, and it's the Prosecution position that, as a matter of law, the accused can no longer represent himself. We're also pointing out that there's been continued breaches by the accused, and one of the things that the accused has been ordered to do was report to Trial Chamber III [sic] about what steps he has taken to withdraw certain material from the internet. He did not do so within the dead-line he was given. And it is also my understanding that, at least as of yesterday, the material has not been removed from the internet. So that is simply to update Your Honours on the status of some of the points or two points we have raised in the supplement. That is all I had for today, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, I look at the transcript, maybe there is an interpretation mistake, line 10, page 23, you talked about Trial Chamber III, were you maybe thinking of Trial Chamber II?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I probably made a mistake, yes, Your Honour. It is Trial Chamber II of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Very well, Mr. Seselj, you have the floor, and after that the hearing will be resumed [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the conviction against me or the decision that was handed down consists of two parts. One part deals with my 15-month sentence; and the second part is the order for me to withdraw the book from my internet site. I don't know whether you are familiar with the decision of the Trial Chamber. The withdrawal of my book from my site is something that is harmful for me and I deny the Trial Chamber's right to try me for contempt of court based on the rules that were passed by the Trial Chamber. This cannot be done even by the Roman court. I'm going to include that in my appeal. However, the sentence is not final and I will not act upon it before it does become final. I announced my appeal and one of my -- the grounds for appeal concerns the illegal request for the book to be removed from my internet site. The book has been published, it has not been banned. If there has been a ban imposed on the distribution of that book, then the book would have to be removed from all the libraries and burned. The book has not been banned and it will remain on my site. If I have indeed disclosed the name of protective witnesses, which I didn't, then this is possibly something that has already been done. Somebody who has committed the crime of murder and is convicted of murder cannot be imposed the obligation to bury the body. I don't think that this is possible. Maybe it can be done at the Hague Tribunal. Be it as it may, I was given a deadline, the 7th or the 8th of August, to remove my book and the decision is still not final. And I'm not removing my book for as long as the decision is not final. When it is going to be final, we shall see. I have until the 1st of November to file my appeal. Today or tomorrow I will file my request for the exemption of two Judges, Meron and Pocar, from the Appeals Chamber. I have drafted my explanation on 40 pages, but that cannot be an argument for me to have a Defence counsel imposed. The argument is he has not complied with a decision that is still not final. I'm asking you what kind of schools you finished, what kind of professors did you have, what kind of text books did you learn from? I find this astonishing. As a professor of law school, I would fail students like you are. They would never pass any exams with me if they had acted and reasoned as you do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Everything has been said. We will see each other again in the month of October as soon as we have a date. I hope that we will see each other shortly, since every hearing is useful. And one should not despair, sometimes things take time. But I'm hopeful. So we will adjourn now, and the Registrar will let you know ahead of time of the new date so that you may get -- you may prepare yourself. I thank you all the parties present. The hearing is adjourned.
